english: Let $S$ be the set of all real numbers $x>0$, $x\neq1$, for which the infinite series
is convergent and its sum is equal to $\log_{1/2}(4x)$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\sum_{x\in S}\log_2x$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $S$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x>0$, $x\neq1$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए अनंत श्रेणी
अभिसारी है तथा इसका योग $\log_{1/2}(4x)$ के बराबर है। तब $\displaystyle\sum_{x\in S}\log_2x$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Put $t=\log_2x\ (t\neq0)$: $\log_x4=\dfrac2t$, so the series is a GP with ratio $r=-\dfrac2t$
Convergent iff $|r|<1\iff|t|>2$; then the sum is $\dfrac{1}{1+\frac2t}=\dfrac{t}{t+2}$
solution_full: The series $1-\dfrac2t+\left(\dfrac2t\right)^{2}-\cdots$ is a geometric series with first term $1$ and common ratio $r=-\dfrac2t$.
An infinite GP converges iff $|r|<1$, i.e. $\left|\dfrac2t\right|<1\iff|t|>2$; its sum is then $\dfrac{1}{1-r}=\dfrac{1}{1+\frac2t}=\dfrac{t}{t+2}$.
By the power and product rules, $\log_{1/2}(4x)=-\log_2(4x)=-(2+t)$.
$t=-1$ ($x=\dfrac12$): $|t|=1<2$; the ratio is $r=2$ and the series $1+2+4+\cdots$ diverges. The formal value $\dfrac{t}{t+2}=-1$ equals $\log_{1/2}2=-1$, but this is not a sum; rejected.
So $S=\left\{\dfrac1{16}\right\}$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{x\in S}\log_2x=-4$ (keeping the divergent case would give $-5$).
originality_note: New: an infinite GP whose ratio is a variable-base logarithm, equated to another logarithm; the convergence condition |log_x 4| < 1 removes the root x = 1/2 at which the formal sum formula still 'works' (way 5). Closest known: sum of infinite GP with ratio log_x a and equations log_x a + log_a x = c. Different because: the extraneous root satisfies the closed-form equation exactly and is removed only by the convergence condition.

concept_use.Logarithmic identities: product, quotien: Change of base gives log_x 4 = 2/t and the power/product rules give log_{1/2}(4x) = -(2+t).
concept_use.Geometric Progression (GP) & Sum of GP: The series is an infinite GP with ratio -2/t; its sum 1/(1-r) and the convergence condition |r| < 1 decide the solution set.

justification: Change of base and the infinite-GP sum lead to a quadratic; the convergence condition removes a root that satisfies the closed-form equation, a trap students fall into. Two ideas linked, numerical answer; above 2024-P1-Q8 (L2).
